answer: To resist Sybil attacks, a network can enforce a cryptographic stake burning curve where registering the n-th identity requires burning stake proportional to n squared. A malicious swarm attempting to forge a safe haven on the network faces superlinear quadratic cost scaling. This protocol barrier pushes adversaries off the economic ledge before they can simulate legitimate identity clusters. Malicious identity creation becomes as fleeting and cost-prohibitive as chasing a blazing comet across the decentralized ledger.
